+A template uses `v-on` (or `@`) or `v-model` on a server component. Server components render on the server only and ship no JavaScript for themselves, so they never emit events and cannot update a `v-model` binding. The listener is never called.

+This warning is reported unless [`experimental.templateDiagnostics`](/docs/guide/going-further/experimental-features#templatediagnostics) is disabled. `@error` is not reported: a server component emits `error` when it fails to load.

+Render the interactive part on the client. You can pair the server component with a `.client.vue` component of the same name, render an interactive child with the `nuxt-client` attribute (with `experimental.componentIslands.selectiveClient` enabled), or move the listener to a client component that wraps the server component.

+A template passes a function, a class or a class instance (such as `new Date()`) as a prop to a server component, or in the `props` or `context` of a `<NuxtIsland>`. Props of a server component are serialized as JSON and sent to the server to render it, so these values cannot reach the component intact.

+This warning is reported unless [`experimental.templateDiagnostics`](/docs/guide/going-further/experimental-features#templatediagnostics) is disabled. Only values that can be seen in the template are checked: inline functions, `new` expressions, and functions or classes declared at the top level of `<script setup>`.
+Pass only JSON-serializable values (strings, numbers, booleans, `null`, arrays and plain objects), and move the logic that needs the function into the server component:
+If the component needs a function from its parent, render it on the client instead of as a server component.
+A template contains a `<NuxtLink>` with a static `to` (or `href`) that does not match any page route, so following the link would show a 404 page.

+This warning is reported unless [`experimental.templateDiagnostics`](/docs/guide/going-further/experimental-features#templatediagnostics) is disabled. Only static, absolute paths are checked: links with a bound `:to`, external URLs, relative paths, hash-only and query-only links, and links with the `external` prop are not. Dynamic route segments and catch-all routes match any value, and paths that a route rule redirects are accepted.
+A path that only matches as the prefix of a route is reported: with only `app/pages/users/[id].vue`, a link to `/users` has no page to render.
